title: Athletics and a bad-tempered Jerry Gray on the road
summary: He boasts of his athleticism and recalls Jerry Gray forcing the radio band on the road.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I don't feel good... You'd never think I was an athlete, would you? I was a slam-bang tennis player, volleyball, roofball(?), everything, swimming... I used to swim across lakes and everything. Did the Australian Crawl without stopping, all the way across. Spirit Lake, that's one big lake. You could take a boat, you know, have a guy row.
But then, music. Puts a stop to everything. Except there's one time I was on the road with Jerry Gray... He made us go on the road; he held the job over our head, the

radio show. So we all had to go. And he paid us all a hundred dollars a week. That's great, isn't it? That's before he went to the psychiatrist and became a good guy. He became just a wonderful person. But up to there, he was known as a horse's ass, and I mean a horse's... There's worse language than that in these tapes.
Well, he was a real horse's ass.
